title: Wegovy (semaglutide): EPAR product information, Annex I summary of product characteristics
journal: European Medicines Agency, EPAR product information for Wegovy, PDF created 13 August 2026; first authorisation 6 January 2022
result: Section 4.4 warns of pulmonary aspiration with general anaesthesia or deep sedation, dehydration from nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea that in rare cases deteriorates renal function, acute pancreatitis, and non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION): epidemiological data indicate an increased risk, no time interval after treatment start has been identified, sudden loss of vision should lead to ophthalmological examination and semaglutide should be stopped if NAION is confirmed. Not recommended below an eGFR of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Women of childbearing potential are recommended to use contraception; semaglutide should not be used in pregnancy or breast-feeding and should be stopped at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy. Table 3 frequencies: NAION very rare (under 1 in 10,000); intestinal obstruction, covering ileus and small intestinal obstruction, frequency not known, from post-marketing reports; acute pancreatitis and delayed gastric emptying uncommon; cholelithiasis, hair loss, hypoglycaemia and diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes common; anaphylaxis rare. Adjudicated acute pancreatitis 0.2% against under 0.1% on placebo in phase 3a trials and 0.2% against 0.3% in SELECT. Cholelithiasis 1.6% with cholecystitis 0.6%, against 1.1% and 0.3%. Pulse rise of 10 beats per minute or more at any time in 67.0% against 50.1%. Epidemiological studies suggest about a two-fold relative risk of NAION in type 2 diabetes, about one additional case per 10,000 person-years. Cholelithiasis in adolescents 3.8% against 0%. Patients with gastroparesis may have more serious gastrointestinal effects.
